sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: All L1 gold records report oral bioavailability values or qualitative extents above the F>=20% threshold, with numeric values from about 45% to about 108% and qualitative reports of complete or very good absorption; no L1 record reports F<20%.

L4 intestinal absorption and permeability records for steroid-like molecules show high fraction absorbed (hydrocortisone 89-95% and fa=0.90; prednisolone 95%; corticosterone complete), high permeability (megestrol acetate BCS class II), and complete absorption of danazol solution in dogs; these support the absorption component for a lipophilic steroid query.

L5 gut-wall records show high passive permeability and no significant efflux for steroid-like molecules (hydrocortisone, budesonide, testosterone), with budesonide efflux ratio ~1 and high Papp; this supports the absence of a gut-wall efflux barrier for the query class.

The estrone P-gp efflux record (efflux ratio ~6.6 in MDR1-MDCK, collapsed to 1.2 with GG918) is a single related-steroid observation with uncertain transfer to the query; efflux alone is not threshold-relevant and does not affirm F<20%.

No supplied record provides affirmative threshold-relevant evidence of F<20% for the query; the unfavorable solubility prior is estimated from logP/ionization rather than measured, and the F>=20% threshold may be met with high permeability even if solubility is limited.

L5 records are for other steroid-like molecules (hydrocortisone, budesonide, testosterone, estrone, artemisinin); transfer to the query is indirect.

Query aqueous solubility and dissolution are not experimentally measured; high logP suggests a limitation but does not establish F<20%.
Whether the query is a P-gp substrate is unknown; the estrone efflux observation is not directly transferable.
